nonvacuity: The specified five-unit experiment has two distinct assignments, both with one treated variant unit and all three fixed units untreated. The conditional support is the same two assignments. Both rank-square sums equal 2, and both statistics equal 1. At alpha=1/20 the printed rejection probability is 1 and the corrected probability is 0. Support nonemptiness and the no-effect schedule are checked in scratch/Check.lean; exact distances and rank calculations are independently checked in scratch/referee_checks.py.

The ten constant-outcome units have 10 original assignments and 6 compatible assignments; the conditioning event has probability 3/5 and each conditional atom has probability 1/6. The distance rank-square sums are 5 or 9/2 and the outcome rank-square sum is 9/2. Every nearest-treated set contains one unit. The lower tails are (1,1,1,1/2,1/3,1/3), and at alpha=1/20 the printed and corrected sizes are 1/2 and 0. Lean verifies nonempty support and no interference; independent exact arithmetic verifies all six rows.

scratch/Check.lean constructs a FiniteLaw on Fin 3 with masses (1/4,0,3/4), verifies nonnegativity and total mass 1, and checks probability(True)=1. Any real statistic on this law is permitted, for example f=(0,1,2), at alpha=1/20. The finite-support cumulative-mass argument gives both super-uniform tails, and the union bound gives both valid rules. The included T1 instance witnesses strict printed-rule inclusion with positive rank variances. Independent checks cover 7260 finite-law instances, including ties and zero masses.

The five-unit instance from T1 satisfies the no-interference null, has a nonempty uniform compatible set and a defined Spearman statistic, and at alpha=1/20 has printed rejection probability 1>alpha. It therefore refutes the stated universal assertion within the paper's intended setting. The Lean theorem is its negation, not a proof of the false printed assertion.

The genuine constant-outcome ten-unit design has nonempty conditional support of size 6 and positive rank variances. Treatment at unit 2 gives -1/sqrt(90), while treatment at unit 5 gives -5/6, so the statistic varies although all outcomes are fixed. The two smallest-statistic assignments give observed lower-tail p=1/3. For the separate constant-statistic implication, use a singleton finite set and t=0, giving p=1. These are conclusions about feasible instances, not contradictory premises.

Use N=3, all 8 assignments, fixed index 0, observed assignment (false,false,false), and Y_i(z)=i+2*Z_i in zero-based indices. The conditional set has 4 assignments, no interference holds, and the fixed outcome is constant despite nonzero direct effects. These facts are compiled in scratch/Check.lean. Any real g is allowed. The separately included ten-unit example has two unequal actual statistics under the fixed-outcome null.

The compiled three-unit instance uses all assignments, a nonempty fixed subset, nonempty variant subset, an observed assignment in the design, and Y_i(z)=i+2*Z_i. Its compatible set has 4 assignments; it satisfies no interference and the fixed-outcome null while exhibiting direct effects. For the variation implication, instead set the fixed unit's outcome to the treatment of a variant unit: two compatible assignments then have the same own treatment and different fixed outcomes, which directly violates NoInterference.

All six table distance vectors and the outcome vector have positive rank variance. The ordering pair (1,2,1,1) and (0,2,1,1), against (1,3,2,1), has squared correlations 2/3 and 25/36 but printed values 8/9 and 20/27. The weakly monotone pair (1,2,3),(0,0,1) has positive rank-square sums 2 and 3/2 and squared correlation 3/4. Independent exact arithmetic verifies all three counterexamples; Lean verifies the weak-pair and outcome rank-square sums.

Take n=3, a=(1,2,3), b=(0,0,1). Both Nonconstant predicates are compiled, and the rank-square sums are 2 and 3/2, so rho=sqrt(3)/2 uses a positive denominator. For the equality cases use b=a or b=(3,2,1). The theorem's positive-divisor identity applies in particular to m=3 and m=2 and is correctly valid for every m>0. Exact checks cover 6696 nonconstant vector pairs with varied tie patterns; the general bound and characterization are the ordinary Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and its nonzero equality case.

Take three units at positions 0,1,2 and d_ij=|i-j|. Lean verifies positive off-diagonal distances and that the partial quotient of 0 by 0 is none. The corrected sums then have positive denominators. At d=1, K=4/9 and K(2)/K(1)=1/4. Non-exponentiality follows because equality to A*exp(-c*d) would force exp(-c)=1/4 and exp(-2*c)=1/4, contradicting exp(-2*c)=exp(-c)^2. The divergence bound uses only B>0,d>0, and the exponential limit follows from continuity at 0. The arbitrary-positive-array generalization includes this genuine metric instance.

Take U={0,1,2}, F={0}, C={1}, T={2}; the union and all three disjointness hypotheses hold. Every proposed repaired quadruple has positive group sizes summing to its total and can be realized by consecutive disjoint finite intervals. The impossible printed quadruple is a conclusion, not an inconsistent premise. Both subtractions of the printed constants have nonnegative intermediate results, so natural truncation is irrelevant.

Use the compiled three-unit direct-effect schedule, all 8 assignments, fixed index 0, and observed fixed treatment false. The compatible set has 4 assignments. With g(y,z)=Z_1, the two statistic values 0 and 1 each have multiplicity 2, so the attained p values are 1/2 and 1 with rejection probabilities exactly 1/2 and 1 at those levels. The zero included in the greatest-element set handles every threshold below the smallest p, including negative thresholds. No zero-cardinality division is needed.

Take N=5, M=2, own index 0 and neighbors={1,2}. The unconditional, own-treated and own-untreated supports have cardinalities 10,4,6. The exposure means are 4/5,1/2,1, so both strict comparisons hold. Lean verifies all three supports are nonempty and the neighborhood hypotheses. Exact enumeration checks 894 neighbor/design instances for N=2 through 7, including M=0 and M=N; no conditional mean is asserted when its support is empty.

The actual adjacency model at observed treatment unit 7 gives outcomes (1,2,2,2,2,3,2,3,2,1), fixed outcomes (1,3,2,1), and fixed distances (6,1,2,3). The conditional design has 6 assignments, all with a treated variant unit and positive rank variances. Holding the observed fixed outcomes constant gives the six stated reference correlations; exactly the assignments treating unit 6 or 7 have reference statistic at most the observed value, giving 2/6=1/3. Independent exact arithmetic verifies the actual observations and every table row. No no-interference hypothesis is imposed on the actual interfering model.

For C=4,M=3 the unique feasible maximum is f=2, with objective 12. For C=5,M=3 exactly f=2,3 maximize the objective at 18. For C=1,M=1 both f=0,1 maximize it at 0, as the odd case says. These satisfy the positive-count premises. Completion of the square gives the universal real identity, and nearest feasible integers to C/2 give the exact integer cases. Enumeration confirms 150 positive C,M instances, including both boundaries and parities.
